 Learn more HBT Financial (HBT) drew fresh attention after third quarter 2026 earnings, reporting net income of US$31.39 million and earnings of US$0.86 per share from continuing operations. 
 The earnings surprise has fed into the share price, with HBT Financial closing at US$37.21 after a 1-day share price return of 2.68% and a year-to-date share price return of 44.73%. The 1-year total shareholder return of 56.66% points to strong longer term momentum. 
 Capitalize on HBT Financial's earnings momentum by reviewing a curated set of bank and financial stocks that pair solid fundamentals with similar price action in the 30 resilient stocks with low risk scores . 
 Bulls point to double digit net income growth and a long record as a community lender. Bears see a fast rising share price and question whether HBT Financial already reflects the good news. The numbers give a clearer signal next. 
 Preferred P/E of 17.4x: Is it justified for HBT Financial? 
 HBT Financial last closed at $37.21, and on a P/E multiple of 17.4x it is priced above several valuation markers that many investors watch for banks. The share price also sits at a discount of 9.2% to the $41 analyst target and 51% below one internal fair value estimate based on future cash flows, which sends a mixed message on how rich the current multiple might be. 
 The P/E ratio compares what you pay per share to the earnings that HBT Financial generates per share and is a common way to frame listed banks. For a lender with forecast earnings growth of 27.9% per year and revenue growth of 19.8% per year, a higher earnings multiple can indicate that the market is already baking in a strong improvement in profitability and return on equity. 
 Here the valuation signals pull in different directions. On one hand, HBT Financial is described as trading at 51% below an estimate of future cash flow value of $75.98, which points to a generous buffer on a discounted cash flow basis. On the other hand, the same stock is called expensive on a P/E of 17.4x compared with a fair P/E of 15.8x derived from regression analysis, which suggests the market may already be paying up relative to a level it could move toward if expectations cool. 
 Against sector peers the premium is even clearer. The P/E of 17.4x is flagged as expensive compared with both the US Banks industry average of 11.5x and a peer group average of 11.7x, which means investors are currently accepting a materially higher price tag per dollar of earnings than for comparable banking stocks.

 Still, a sharp reversal in HBT Financial's premium P/E, or a setback in its community banking franchise, could quickly puncture the recent momentum story.

 Another View: SWS DCF model paints a different picture for HBT Financial 
 While the P/E of 17.4x frames HBT Financial as expensive against peers, the SWS DCF model points the other way. On that cash flow view, an estimated value of $75.98 per share versus a $37.21 price suggests the stock is trading at a steep discount. Which signal do you trust more: today's earnings multiple or a longer term cash flow view?
